Reading the connections

A heteroclinic orbit leaves one saddle and approaches another. A homoclinic orbit leaves and returns to the same saddle.

The blue stable branches approach a saddle in forward time; the orange unstable branches leave it. A connection is highlighted in pink at its critical parameter.

x′ = 0: y = ±√(x² + 1)y′ = 0: y = x² + a

Connections are limiting orbits: their endpoints are reached only as t → ±∞. The heteroclinic value has an exact algebraic formula; the homoclinic value is a numerical shooting estimate. Computed paths stop at the integration time or escape boundary.

Explore planar bifurcations

This family changes with a single parameter a. The portrait, nullclines, fixed points, and equilibrium diagram update together.

  • Start at a connection. Choose Heteroclinic or Homoclinic, then use Before and After to compare a ± δ. Change δ for a closer look. The heteroclinic joins two different saddles; the homoclinic loops back to one saddle.
  • Read the nullclines. On the cool gray curves x′ = 0, so the field is vertical. On the warm gray parabola y′ = 0, so it is horizontal. Intersections are equilibria.
  • Follow the saddle branches. Blue branches approach a saddle, orange branches leave it. Arrow direction always means forward time, even though stable branches are computed backwards. Pink highlights a connection only at its critical value.
  • Explore other transitions. Equilibria meet at a = −1 and a = 1. At the subcritical Hopf value a ≈ 0.868034, the upper-left equilibrium loses stability. A small unstable periodic orbit exists just below this value.
  • Add initial points. Click the phase portrait or use the coordinate fields. Added points stay in place as you vary a. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, or use the view buttons. Both time directions are drawn.
  • Use the diagram. Click or drag horizontally to set a. The arrow keys change a by 0.01; hold Shift for 0.001. The equilibrium curves show x versus a, not the extent of periodic orbits.

The homoclinic value is found by matching the saddle’s stable and unstable branches on a transverse section. Its displayed loop joins these two computed halves to avoid long-time numerical drift. The exact heteroclinic line is y = mx − 1/(2m), where m³ − m − 1 = 0 and a = −m − 1/(4m).
